prediction_vs_result.predicted: Each group's overlap agrees with its left-out members, and the two overlaps differ before the first wrong calculation at some stretch of merges rather than everywhere.
observed: Before the first wrong token there are 120 reference positions with at least two answers in each group (opening 5, initial state 65, descent 50). 115 of them hold main-wording answers only: the four correct block answers and seven failures (cart, sled, bead, coaster). The other-wording answers align at 7 to 18 positions and add almost nothing.
Each group's overlap is strong: a left-out answer agrees with its own group's overlap at cosine 0.96 to 0.98 at every depth.
The discrepancy between the two overlaps keeps its direction when any member is left out (cosine 0.95 to 0.96 at every depth).

A left-out answer falls on its own side of the discrepancy in 59 to 62 percent of position-and-merge cells for the failures and, in the main wording, 0.80 to 0.89 for three block answers and 0.31 for block-m2-changed; sled 0.76, coaster 0.81, cart 0.63, bead-changed 0.39.

In 2,914 of 12,600 cells every left-out answer falls on its own side. They sit at 81 positions, 40 in the initial state and 41 in the descent. At some positions nearly all 105 merges qualify: the header of the state after the descent, and the statement that names the descent's potential energy, which the correct answers call gained and the failures call lost.

By depth the discrepancy is largest at the feed-forward merges of layers 9 to 13 and the attention merge of layer 14. Left-out answers fall on their own side most often around layers 14 to 17 (0.55 to 0.57). There is no sharp location.
not_predicted: The naming of the descent energy as lost comes before the first wrong operator and already separates the groups.
Positions that hold the questions' own numbers also qualify as fully separating, which shows question content inside the discrepancy.

failures_only.scope: Original model only. No edit in this run.

what_this_changes: Steps 1 to 3 exist for round one's questions in the form the method asks for: full traces, group overlaps, the discrepancy with each member left out.

On round one's own questions the discrepancy cannot be told apart from the object: every main-wording correct answer is the block question and every failure of this group is another object. What recurs across members is therefore partly the question.
